gap: No result ChatGPT got lists, in Sonos's own words, which Sonos speakers can pass a Bluetooth turntable's audio to the rest of a Sonos system: Arc Ultra, Beam Ultra, Era 100, Era 100 SL, Era 300, Move 2, Roam 2, Roam SL and Sonos Play. The original Roam can't. Bluetooth is turned off on a portable speaker that is set up as a surround, and the speaker has to be on Wi-Fi first and stay grouped.
standout_why: Compared against turntableverse.com/best-bluetooth-turntables (rank 1–2 in both chats). It only says that, per Sonos, 'its Bluetooth-capable speakers can pair with a Bluetooth turntable'. It doesn't name which Sonos models can share Bluetooth audio with a group, and it doesn't mention the Roam exception, the surround-mode shutoff or the requirement to stay grouped. It also lists Era 100/300 and Move 2 only under wired line-in, which suggests Bluetooth isn't a route for those speakers. ChatGPT itself offered 'Sonos or other wireless home audio system' as a follow-up without answering it. I could not read the body of the cited What Hi-Fi? page (the fetch returned only the title). vinylpickup.com failed on a TLS error. I didn't open the cited Louder page, so I'm scoring a 2 rather than a 3.
decides: This confirms rather than changes the pick. Any of ChatGPT's three Bluetooth-output decks (AT-LP70XBT, Sony PS-LX3BT, JBL Spinner BT) works for a Sonos owner who has one of the listed models. That speaker receives the turntable over Bluetooth and passes it to the grouped Sonos rooms. A shopper with only an original Roam can't share the turntable to other rooms. A Move 2 or Roam that is set up as a surround drops its Bluetooth. Sonos owners with none of the listed models need a wired line-in route instead. On the Audio-Technica, Bluetooth pairing requires the built-in preamp switch to be on LINE. That means the Bluetooth path always uses the deck's own preamp, not an external phono stage.

findings.label: Sonos products that can share Bluetooth audio with other Sonos products
findings.value: Arc Ultra, Beam Ultra, Era 100, Era 100 SL, Era 300, Move 2, Roam, Roam 2, Roam SL, Sonos Play
findings.source_title: Share Bluetooth audio with your Sonos system (Sonos Support)
findings.note: Sonos's own support article (en-US). The original Move isn't on the list; only Move 2 is.

findings.label: Sonos exception: products that can't swap Bluetooth audio with other Sonos products
findings.value: Roam (original), Sonos Ace, Sonos Ace Ultra
findings.source_title: Share Bluetooth audio with your Sonos system (Sonos Support)
findings.note: The page puts Roam on the sharing list but says Roam, Ace and Ace Ultra 'cannot swap Bluetooth audio' to or from other Sonos products. So a turntable paired to an original Roam plays on that Roam only.

findings.label: Sonos Bluetooth sharing requirements
findings.value: The speaker must be set up and connected to the Sonos system over Wi-Fi, and must stay grouped to keep sharing. Bluetooth is disabled on portables set up as surrounds.
findings.source_title: Share Bluetooth audio with your Sonos system (Sonos Support)
findings.note: Sonos wording: 'Bluetooth functionality is disabled' when a supported portable is set up as surrounds.

findings.label: Pre-amp switch setting required for Bluetooth pairing
findings.source_title: Pairing a Bluetooth device – AT-LP70XBT online user manual (Audio-Technica)
findings.note: Maker's online manual, step 2: 'Set the pre-amplifier selector switch to the LINE side.' Step 3 names the target as 'a Bluetooth-supporting device such as headphones or speakers'.

findings.label: Bluetooth pairing distance and pairing-mode timeout
findings.value: within 1 m (3.3 ft) for pairing; pairing mode ends after about 120 s
findings.source_title: Pairing a Bluetooth device – AT-LP70XBT online user manual (Audio-Technica)
findings.note: The manual also says Audio-Technica 'cannot guarantee the operation of connected Bluetooth devices'. The unit has no power switch and draws standby current.
